title: HTTP/3 WebSocket TCP Forwarder Buffering Architecture
purpose: Define bounded TCP response chunk forwarding for accepted RFC 9220 WebSocket TCP tunnels.
design_summary: `Http3WebSocketTcpForwarderOptions.BufferSize` names the TCP read buffer used by `Http3WebSocketTcpForwarder` when returning TCP bytes as binary WebSocket messages. The forwarder awaits each WebSocket write before reading the next TCP chunk, so WebSocket stream backpressure limits TCP-to-WebSocket progression instead of buffering an unbounded TCP response in memory.
data_and_state_considerations: The options object is read at forwarding start and converted to the existing positive buffer-size path. Each TCP read owns one reusable buffer, and each emitted WebSocket binary frame carries at most the configured chunk size.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Non-positive buffer sizes are rejected before forwarding starts.
The helper does not implement TCP target authorization, DNS resolution, or production proxy routing policy.
The bounded chunk proof is local loopback stress proof, not external peer interoperability.
risks: Very small buffers increase frame count and control overhead.
Very large buffers increase per-forwarder memory use, so callers should choose a value that fits their proxy workload.
